title: 只是隔壁邻居  (Only the Neighbour Next Door)

segments.t: At ten o'clock Tuesday night at Courtyard Inn, Qing, Chen, and Manager Zhou hurry to the front door expecting an early visit from City Hall—and find their next-door neighbour smiling on the step instead. Listen first.
呼！我的心差点儿跳过了院子里的树！
原来只是隔壁书店老板帮我们送信！
小晴，快读读她递给你的市政厅盖章信封。
“街坊老建筑咖啡馆审核——星期三下午三点整。”
谢天谢地，不是今晚！小晴，快念里面的检查清单！
第一条：门口招牌清楚，院子向街坊邻居敞开。
大门上了油，木头招牌也刷好了——没问题。
第二条：室内座位明亮安全，有新鲜热茶和点心。
十二把椅子、干净窗户、新铜电线——还有两个神秘白罐子！
小晴，睡觉以前先把那两个罐子贴上标签。
左边这勺是甜的！右边这勺像海水一样咸！都贴上大红标签！
危机解除！大家快去睡觉——早上六点很快就到！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
呼！我的心差点儿跳过了院子里的树！

'Phew! My heart nearly jumped over the courtyard tree!' Manager Zhou lets out a huge breath of relief. The spoken chunk for "nearly" literally says "missed by a tiny bit", which you can drop in before almost any close call.
原来只是隔壁书店老板帮我们送信！

'Turns out it was only the bookshop owner next door bringing our mail!' Qing opens with the handy word for "as it turns out", built from the word for "original". Notice how "bookshop" simply joins "book" and "shop", while "next door" literally means "separated by a wall".
小晴，快读读她递给你的市政厅盖章信封。

'Read the stamped City Hall envelope she handed you, Qing.' Chen doubles the word for "read" to make his request sound brisk and friendly rather than stern. Mandarin builds "envelope" out of "letter" plus "seal".
“街坊老建筑咖啡馆审核——星期三下午三点整。”

'"Neighbourhood Heritage Cafe Review—Wednesday at three o'clock sharp."' At the very end of the time expression, the single word for "whole" works just like English "sharp" or "on the dot" after an hour.
谢天谢地，不是今晚！小晴，快念里面的检查清单！
'Thank goodness, not tonight! Read the checklist inside, Qing!' Zhou's four-word cry of relief literally thanks heaven and thanks earth—the everyday Mandarin twin of "thank goodness!"
第一条：门口招牌清楚，院子向街坊邻居敞开。

'Item one: a clear sign at the gate, and the courtyard open to neighbours.' To count rules or checklist items in Mandarin, you pair the number with a word that originally meant a long strip of bamboo where official lines were written.
大门上了油，木头招牌也刷好了——没问题。
'Gate oiled, wooden sign painted—all set.' Chen finishes with a handy two-word phrase that means "no problem", doubling nicely as a crisp "check!" when ticking off a list.
第二条：室内座位明亮安全，有新鲜热茶和点心。

'Item two: bright, safe indoor seating, with fresh hot tea and pastries.' Look how transparent these two-piece words are: "indoor" is "room-inside", and "pastries" literally means "dot the heart"—a little snack to touch your appetite.
十二把椅子、干净窗户、新铜电线——还有两个神秘白罐子！
'Twelve chairs, clean windows, new copper wire—and two mystery white jars!' Mandarin uses a dedicated counter meaning "grasped handle" for chairs, because you take hold of the back to move one.
小晴，睡觉以前先把那两个罐子贴上标签。
'Label those two jars right now before anyone sleeps, Qing.' Unlike English, Mandarin says "sleep before" rather than "before sleeping"—the time signpost always stands at the end of its phrase.
左边这勺是甜的！右边这勺像海水一样咸！都贴上大红标签！
'Left spoon—sweet! Right spoon—salty as the sea! Big red labels on both!' To build "as salty as seawater", Mandarin sets "like seawater" first and lands on "the same salty" at the end.
危机解除！大家快去睡觉——早上六点很快就到！

'Crisis averted! Everyone off to bed—six in the morning comes fast!' Manager Zhou opens with a crisp four-character expression meaning "danger lifted", the natural Mandarin way to say "crisis averted!"
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.
呼！我的心差点儿跳过了院子里的树！
原来只是隔壁书店老板帮我们送信！
小晴，快读读她递给你的市政厅盖章信封。
“街坊老建筑咖啡馆审核——星期三下午三点整。”
谢天谢地，不是今晚！小晴，快念里面的检查清单！
第一条：门口招牌清楚，院子向街坊邻居敞开。
大门上了油，木头招牌也刷好了——没问题。
第二条：室内座位明亮安全，有新鲜热茶和点心。
十二把椅子、干净窗户、新铜电线——还有两个神秘白罐子！
小晴，睡觉以前先把那两个罐子贴上标签。
左边这勺是甜的！右边这勺像海水一样咸！都贴上大红标签！
危机解除！大家快去睡觉——早上六点很快就到！
Sugar and salt are clearly labelled in red, the checklist is clear, and Wednesday morning's six-o'clock kitchen shift awaits. See you next time.
明天见！
